prompt: Why are epoxides much more reactive than typical ethers?

options.label: The 3-membered ring stores ~27 kcal/mol of angle strain, released upon ring opening
The C-O bonds in epoxides are more polarized than in acyclic ethers
The ring-opened form is resonance-stabilized, which lowers the activation barrier
The oxygen in an epoxide carries a formal positive charge, making it electrophilic

explanation: Epoxides have severe angle strain (60° vs 109.5° ideal for sp³) plus torsional strain = ~27 kcal/mol stored energy. Breaking the ring RELEASES that → huge driving force. Even weak nucleophiles can open them. Normal ethers have no strain and are inert.
